Firing a trigger event periodically vs. one time
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
You can use the /whisk.system/alarms/once to feed configures the Alarm service to fire a trigger event one time on a specified date. On the other hand , you will need to use /whisk.system/alarms/interval to feed configures the Alarm service to fire a trigger event on an interval-based schedule. 
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
A one-time trigger uses the `/whisk.system/alarms/once` feed and fires on a specified date. For example:
`ibmcloud fn trigger create fireOnce --feed /whisk.system/alarms/once --param date "2019-12-25T12:30:00.000Z" --param trigger_payload "{\"name\":\"Odin\",\"place\":\"Asgard\"}" --param deleteAfterFire "rules"` [S3][S4]

A periodic trigger uses the `/whisk.system/alarms/interval` feed and fires repeatedly according to an interval-based schedule. [S4]

 Firing a trigger event one time 

The /whisk.system/alarms/once feed configures the Alarm service to fire a trigger event one time on a specified date. To create a fire-once alarm, run the following command.

ibmcloud fn trigger create fireOnce --feed /whisk.system/alarms/once --param date "2019-12-25T12:30:00.000Z" --param trigger_payload "{"name":"Odin","place":"Asgard"}" --param deleteAfterFire "rules"
